newsitem.title: CANADA: Martin disappointed, but says data volatile.
newsitem.headline: Martin disappointed, but says data volatile.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin on Friday said a surge in unemployment in September was disappointing but that monthly jobs reports were "volatile."

"There is no doubt that the figures are disappointing. However, we mustn't lose sight of the fact that the monthly data are volatile," Martin told Parliament in response to a question from the opposition Bloc Quebecois.
Earlier on Friday Statistics Canada said Canada's unemployment rate jumped 0.5 percent to an unexpectedly high 9.9 percent in September as the economy lost 47,000 jobs.
The government agency said full-time employment fell by 86,000, wiping out the 72,000-job gain in August and cutting the year's total gains in half. Part-time employment rose by 39,000 in September.
-- Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
